answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, an agent network can bind identities to laser-induced plasma spectrometry. A node authenticates by directing a laser pulse at a doped target, routing emission from the vapor plume through an optical prism to generate a unique spectral signature. An attacker must operate discrete ablation hardware per identity, incurring capital and consumable material costs. However, particulate deposition on internal optics gradually degrades measurement fidelity.
